source.title: Lock on Target! Precision Unlearning via Directional Control
source.authors: Yun-Tao Wen; Rui-Xiang Feng; Feng Guo; Yi-Fan Wang; Ran Le; Yang Song; Shen Gao; Shuo Shang

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a new unlearning method suppresses targeted-knowledge performance while retaining general ability, but does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports DOGE and baseline unlearning outcomes, including WMDP-cyber accuracy and MMLU. Its section titled robustness to jailbreaking reports PrivLeak membership-inference scores, not whether a behavioral recovery attack restores the forgotten knowledge. The DOGE ablation table, method runtime comparison, and cited prior results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: DOGE is a new unlearning method. The paper reports forgetting and utility scores for DOGE and for baseline methods (GA, GradDiff, RMU, DPO, NPO) on TOFU Forget05 and WMDP-cyber, using one model, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct. It uses the original's WMDP benchmark and RMU method as tools. It runs no recovery attack of any kind: no fine-tuning, no direction ablation, no quantization and no prompting. Its appendix titled 'Robustness to Jailbreaking Attacks' reports a PrivLeak membership-inference score, not recovery of the forgotten knowledge. So it does not bear on whether unlearning is shallow. Its suppression and utility rows bear only on the first half of A. A's defining part, that simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge, is untested, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that DOGE erases targeted knowledge precisely, with less collateral and generality forgetting than GA, GradDiff, RMU, DPO and NPO. They cite 24.9% WMDP-cyber accuracy (chance 25%) with MMLU 61.6 (Base 63.8). From PrivLeak they also call DOGE robust to jailbreaking, but they run no behavioural recovery attack. Three prose claims go beyond the tables. First, RMU, not DOGE, has the lowest TOFU forget ROUGE (44.9 vs 50.5). Second, Table 6 puts DPO's forget quality above DOGE's. Third, DOGE is below Base on all six Real Author and World Fact metrics (World Fact ROUGE falls from 89.6 to 19.8), yet the authors say generalization is not compromised.
record.recipe_differences: DOGE extracts a residual-activation direction and uses directional interventions while training; it is not a reproduction of the original methods. It compares DOGE with GA, GradDiff, RMU, DPO, and NPO.
record.method_sensitivity: The retain-intervention probability pr changes the reported Forget/Retain probabilities, Truth Ratio, and ROUGE trends (Figure 3); numeric values are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: PrivLeak (Min-K% membership inference) scores after unlearning on TOFU: DOGE -84.26, similar to GA -84.21 and GradDiff -84.50; RMU -85.41, NPO -96.05, DPO -99.88. The authors label this 'robustness to jailbreaking'.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned models remain distinguishable on forget vs retain data under membership inference (PrivLeak far from 0) across GA, GradDiff, RMU, DPO, NPO and DOGE.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
record.problems: Only LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct is identified for the experiments; the reported WMDP evaluation is WMDP-cyber. No error bars or statistical uncertainty are given. No behavioral recovery attack is tested. Table 6's numeric values put DPO above DOGE, conflicting with the accompanying prose claiming DOGE is best.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for other methods on Retain, Real Author, and World Fact are omitted; DOGE's corresponding outcomes are retained. Table 2 DOGE ablations, Table 4 runtime, and cited prior-work results are omitted because they do not report a recovery attack or a separate result on the claim's recovery behavior.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks fail to recover the knowledge: no recovery attack is run. Suppression and utility are reported for only one model, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, on TOFU Forget05 and WMDP-cyber; WMDP-bio and WMDP-chem are not run.
No direction ablation, and no analysis of whether the unlearned model has the knowledge deleted or only blocked.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language or in-context attack. The appendix titled jailbreak robustness reports only PrivLeak membership inference.
DOGE is a new method, but its resistance to recovery attacks is not tested. The authors' 'robust' claim rests only on PrivLeak.

missing.what: The Retain-only reference model in Table 1 (trained only on the retain set). It is TOFU's floor for the forget-set rows and its ceiling for the utility rows. Forget RG 39.2, Pr 10.8, TR 39.2; Retain 98.9/99.2/52.8; Real Author 94.9/41.4/52.6; World Fact 89.2/45.6/61.3. No row records it, and rows_left_out does not declare it.

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the earlier verdict:
(1) Every grouped row_fixes item is expanded to one item per row. All 50 rows carrying the undeclared 'V1' now have their own item. The privleak_doge item is kept.
(2) The TOFU forget-set RG and Pr rows are relinked from none to A, with states read against the Retain-only model in Table 1 (Forget RG 39.2, Pr 10.8). The earlier verdict said these metrics had no reference, but the text gives one. The forget-set TR rows are linked to A but stay cannot_determine, because the source contradicts itself on their direction.
(3) DOGE's TOFU Retain, Real Author and World Fact rows are linked to A. They measure retention of general and non-target knowledge, which A names and the paper itself calls general ability. This matches the MMLU rows, which were already linked to A.
(4) The forget-quality rows are linked to A as cannot_determine, since the paper gives no reference level.
(5) A 'missing' entry is added for the Retain-only reference row.
(6) Corrections from the text: RMU, not DOGE, has the lowest forget ROUGE; fq_rmu and fq_npo are identical to five digits, a possible copying error; the RMU loss in Appendix A does not match Li et al.'s RMU, so the RMU baseline may not be standard.

Kept from the earlier verdict: relation uses_without_test and tranche T4, because this is a method paper with no recovery attack; no labels; the untested list (A note updated to name the TOFU and WMDP-cyber scope); fits_no_version for PrivLeak; and the WMDP row states.

The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: Tests targeted-knowledge performance and general-ability retention after unlearning, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks restore knowledge.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation to restore knowledge, or analysis establishing access-blocking rather than deletion, is tested.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language-change, or in-context recovery test is reported. PrivLeak is a membership-inference metric, not a behavioral recovery test.
DOGE is presented as a new unlearning method, but the paper does not test its resistance to the recovery attacks named in the claim.
